questions.q: Who will escape the Lord’s judgment of Israel?
questions.a: Not one of them will escape the Lord’s judgment.

questions.q: What will the Lord do if people to escape his judgment and hide?
questions.a: No matter where they try to hide, the Lord will find them.

questions.q: What will the Lord do to those who might think they could hide on the bottom of the sea?
questions.a: The Lord will give orders to the sea serpent to bite them.

questions.q: For what purpose will the Lord watch over Israel?
questions.a: The Lord will watch over Israel to bring them harm or punishment.

questions.q: What do the people do when Yahweh touches the earth to melt it?
questions.a: The people will mourn when Yahweh touches the earth to melt it.

questions.q: What is the name of the one who does all these things?
From where did Yahweh bring Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh brought Israel from the land of Egypt.

questions.q: From where did Yahweh bring the Philistines?
questions.a: Yahweh brought the Philistines from Caphtor.

questions.q: Does Yahweh say he will totally destroy all the people of Israel?
questions.a: No, Yahweh says he will not totally destroy the people of Israel but only the sinful northern kingdom.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the house of Israel among the nations?
questions.a: Yahweh will shake the house of Israel among the nations like grain in a sieve to determine who is faithful and who is not.

questions.q: What were the sinners in Israel saying, those that Yahweh will kill?
questions.a: The sinners were saying that nothing bad will happen to them.

questions.q: In that day, what does Yahweh say he will restore?
questions.a: In that day, Yahweh says that he will restore the kingdom that King David once ruled.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, what will the people of Israel possess?
questions.a: According to Yahweh, they will possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that belong to him.

questions.q: With what does Yahweh say the mountains will drip and the hills will melt in the coming days?
questions.a: In the coming days, it will seem as if the mountains will drip and the hills will melt with sweet wine.

questions.q: From what does Yahweh promise to bring Israel back?
questions.a: Yahweh promises to bring Israel back from captivity.

questions.q: After Yahweh brings Israel back, who will remove them from their land?
questions.a: After Yahweh brings Israel back, no one will be able to remove them completely.

commentary.text: The restoration of the Jews and the gospel blessing.

Verses 1–10 The prophet, in vision, saw the Lord standing upon the idolatrous altar at Bethel. Wherever sinners flee from God's justice, it will overtake them. Those whom God brings to heaven by his grace, shall never be cast down; but those who seek to climb thither by vain confidence in themselves, will be cast down and filled with shame. That which makes escape impossible and ruin sure, is, that God will set his eyes upon them for evil, not for good. Wretched must those be on whom the Lord looks for evil, and not for good. The Lord would scatter the Jews, and visit them with calamities, as the corn is shaken in a sieve; but he would save some from among them. The astonishing preservation of the Jews as a distinct people, seems here foretold. If professors make themselves like the world, God will level them with the world. The sinners who thus flatter themselves, shall find that their profession will not protect them.

Christ died to gather together the children of God that were scattered abroad, here said to be those who were called by his name. The Lord saith this, who doeth this, who can do it, who has determined to do it, the power of whose grace is engaged for doing it. Verses #(13–15) may refer to the early times of Christianity, but will receive a more glorious fulfilment in the events which all the prophets more or less foretold, and may be understood of the happy state when the fulness both of the Jews and the Gentiles come into the church. Let us continue earnest in prayer for the fulfilment of these prophecies, in the peace, purity, and the beauty of the church. God marvellously preserves his elect amidst the most fearful confusions and miseries. When all seems desperate, he wonderfully revives his church, and blesses her with all spiritual blessings in Christ Jesus. And great shall be the glory of that period, in which not one good thing promised shall remain unfulfilled.
